inputs: a disk model with the outer alphabet fixed and an inner arrangement satisfying the two alignments the text prints (outer A against inner G, outer R against inner M)
expected: the two alignments are parsed out of the registered course text at run time (outer A against inner G; outer R maps to inner M) and the inner arrangement is built from those parsed constraints; the model must reproduce both printed mappings, keep them consistent with a single permutation, change the alphabet when the inner disk turns and restore it after a full revolution, must change the substitution alphabet when the inner disk is rotated, and must restore the original alphabet after one full turn
limitations: Only inner[0]=G and inner[17]=M are printed; the other 24 positions are an arbitrary scramble here and no historical arrangement is claimed.

inputs: the letter R - the one the printed mapping names - enciphered under three alignments (0, 5, 11)
expected: the text says one plaintext symbol can now map to many ciphertext symbols depending on its position; three alignments must give three different letters
limitations: Three alignments of one letter; the check shows the mechanism, it does not measure security.

inputs: the same 24-letter block enciphered with a regular alignment rule (0,1,2 repeating) and with an irregular one (0,7,3,19,11,2,23)
expected: Alberti suggested changing at irregular intervals to make the switching harder to detect: an analyst assuming the regular period-3 rule is consistent with itself at 1.000 on the first and materially lower on the second
limitations: A single assumed-period detector on a short block; it demonstrates why the rule matters, it does not prove any particular rule safe.

inputs: a 17-letter block enciphered with alignments cycling 0,4,8 on one inner arrangement, then decrypted with the same and with a different inner arrangement
expected: the source states both parties had to have identical disks: the same arrangement must recover the block, a different one must not
limitations: One round-trip pair; the failure of the wrong disk is the point, not a measure of work factor.
